key_insight: Among cancer patients in Northwest Russia, COVID-19 vaccination was associated with substantially better overall survival.
clinical_relevance: These registry-linked findings suggest vaccination may be an important protective factor in oncology populations, though causality cannot be proven from this observational study.
method: Retrospective population-based cohort using cancer registry, vaccination records, and AI-read chest CT data
1,144 cancer patients with CT scans from Aug 2020 to Apr 2021; landmark analyses used to reduce immortal time bias
Compared vaccinated vs unvaccinated survival with Kaplan-Meier and multivariable Cox models
evidence_signal: Vaccination was associated with higher 3-year overall survival (80.3% vs 45.7%) and a lower adjusted mortality hazard (HR 0.40, 95% CI 0.25-0.64) in the primary landmark analysis.
watch_item: This is an observational registry study with low vaccination coverage and possible residual confounding, so the survival association should not be interpreted as proof of causation.
paper_title: COVID-19 vaccination and survival of cancer patients in Northwestern Russia: a historical registry-based cohort study
